Engine v0.40.0, 1055 features. Every row is enumerated from the repository; its **source** column names the file and line (or the command) it came from. Placement (page, section, Studio control, docs anchor) comes from `placements.toml`; a feature without an entry is listed as UNPLACED.

**Editions.** The engine has no feature gate: every engine feature is Free core (public source: `web/index.html`, the open-core card, and `README.md`, Support & professional services). Pro and Custom-study rows exist only where a public file of the engine repository says so, and each quotes that file.

## Editions at a glance

| Edition | What it is | Public source |
|---|---|---|
| Pro | **Calibrated clock digital twin**. A digital twin of a clock calibrated to the device's published Allan-deviation budget (the standard measure of clock stability). | web/index.html:759 (branch HEAD 7f5e3e39) “clock digital twins calibrated to a device's published Allan budget” |
| Pro | **Architecture trade study ranked on a figure of merit**. Candidate positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) architectures compared and ranked on a single figure of merit. | web/index.html:371 “architecture trade studies ranked on a figure of merit” |
| Pro | **Audit-grade, reproducible evidence pack**. The evidence a review or procurement board asks for, packaged so every figure can be reproduced. | web/index.html:760 (branch HEAD 7f5e3e39) “audit-grade, reproducible evidence packs” |
| Pro | **Model-based systems-engineering and programme tooling**. Model-based systems-engineering (MBSE) and programme tooling that checks a programme's requirements against runs of the open engine and produces a verification cross-reference matrix (VCRM), a Systems Modeling Language version 2 (SysML v2) model, a change-impact report and an offline evidence pack. It reads only what the open engine publishes: each run's result.json and report.json, the scenario file, the field-units schema and the verification matrix's labels. | README.md:1503 “Kshana Pro's model-based systems-engineering (MBSE) and programme tooling checks a programme's requirements against runs of the open engine: it imports requirements as comma-separated values (CSV), or as a documented subset of the Requirements Interchange Format (ReqIF) or of Systems Modeling Language version 2 (SysML v2) text, evaluates each acceptance criterion, with its unit, against the values a run wrote, and produces a verification cross-reference matrix (VCRM), a SysML v2 model, a change-impact report and an offline evidence pack. It re-runs and recomputes nothing, and reads only what the open engine publishes: each run's result.json (the fields a criterion names, their units, the reproducibility stamp of scenario hash, seed, engine version and schema version, and the run's label and figure tiers), its report.json (kind, reproducibility record and capability labels), the scenario file (its hash, kind, seed and parameters), the field-units schema (each field's unit, provenance and evidence tier) and the verification matrix (each capability's VALIDATED, MODELLED or PARTNER label).” |
| Pro | **Kshana Pro is a strict superset of open Kshana**. Pro depends on the open engine as a library and never forks it; every open scenario kind runs in Pro unchanged, adds no physical model, and each Pro figure keeps the tier the open engine gave it. | docs/PRO.md:46 “Pro depends on the open engine as a library and never forks it. Every open scenario kind runs in Pro unchanged, and an open scenario runs in Pro with no licence at all.” |
| Pro | **Design optimiser: the Pareto front of a design space**. The Pareto front of a stated design space over any open scenario kind, its knee, and each front design written out as a plain scenario file whose result the free engine reproduces. | docs/PRO.md:98 “A Pro user states the design space (each variable a scenario setting with its allowed values), the constraints and two or three objectives, and gets the whole Pareto front: the designs that no other design beats on every objective at once.” |
| Pro | **Uncertainty and sensitivity over thousands of runs**. Stated input uncertainties give confidence bands, the probability of meeting a limit and a ranking of the inputs that drive the result (Sobol' indices or standardised regression coefficients); a long study can be stopped and resumed. | docs/PRO.md:142 “A Pro user states how uncertain each input is and gets confidence bands, the probability of meeting a limit, and a ranking of the inputs that drive the result.” |
| Pro | **One-command mission dossier**. Requirements checked against real runs, a verification matrix with its open items, and a PDF (Portable Document Format), HTML (HyperText Markup Language) and JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) dossier in which every number can be re-derived with the free engine. | docs/PRO.md:189 “A Pro user gets one mission dossier in one command: requirements checked against real runs, a verification matrix with its open items, and a PDF in which every number can be re-derived with the free engine.” |
| Pro | **Scenario regression check**. Runs a manifest of scenarios, compares every figure of merit with the previous baseline within a per-figure tolerance, writes an HTML (HyperText Markup Language) report and exits non-zero on a regression. | docs/PRO.md:399 “It writes an HTML report and exits with a non-zero code when a figure regresses, so a continuous-integration pipeline can stop on it.” |
| Pro | **Study dossier**. One scenario written up as a reproducible technical note in HTML (HyperText Markup Language) and JSON (JavaScript Object Notation), with a tier on every figure. | docs/PRO.md:413 “One scenario becomes a reproducible technical note in HTML and JSON: scope, method, results with a tier on every figure, limitations, and the exact scenario text run.” |
| Pro | **On-premises service**. A small Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) service on the customer's own network that reports health, version and kinds and runs a posted scenario; without a licence it serves the open engine only. | docs/PRO.md:419 “Pro can run as a small HTTP service on your own network: it reports its health, its version and the kinds it can run, and runs a scenario posted to it.” |
| Pro | **Campaign watch**. Named figures in a set of scenarios, each with what worse means, gated in a continuous-integration pipeline: Monte Carlo figures judged by statistical tests, every run appended to a hash-chained history, a trend page and a figure-by-figure diff. | docs/PRO.md:246 “A Pro user names the figures that matter in a set of scenarios, says what worse means for each, and gets a pipeline that fails when a change to a scenario, a model or the engine makes one of them worse, or stops meeting its requirement.” |
| Pro | **Spectrum coexistence**. Candidate signal plans tested against every open-service global navigation satellite system (GNSS) signal the engine models, in both directions, over a worldwide grid, with a verdict per plan and signal against a stated limit (a modelled upper bound, not a regulatory finding). | docs/PRO.md:294 “A Pro user tests one or more candidate signal plans, each a signal design and a constellation, against every open-service GNSS signal the engine models, with every satellite of the plan in view at once, and gets a verdict per plan and signal against a limit the study states.” |
| Pro | **On-premises job service**. A job queue on the team's own network that survives a restart, a stored result per job, a job identifier that is the hash of the request, and a hash-chained delivery ledger with a check. | docs/PRO.md:334 “A Pro team queues studies on its own network, lets them run while no one watches, and can show afterwards exactly which result was delivered for which request.” |
| Custom study | **Modelled PNT-resilience study (for example an optimism-gap audit)**. A bespoke, modelled positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) resilience study, reproducible from scenario, seed and engine version, every figure labelled; not a certification. | web/index.html:773 (branch HEAD 7f5e3e39) “PNT-resilience study — e.g. an optimism-gap audit — reproducible from scenario + seed + engine version” |
| Custom study | **Custom sensor and resilience models calibrated to your hardware**. Sensor and resilience models calibrated to the customer's own hardware, maintained in a private overlay. | README.md:1526 “Custom sensor models — calibrated to your hardware, including export-sensitive resilience models maintained in a private overlay.” |
| Custom study | **Export-controlled resilience work under clearance and NDA**. Export-controlled resilience work delivered under the appropriate clearance and non-disclosure agreement (NDA). | web/index.html:766 (branch HEAD 7f5e3e39) “export-controlled resilience work delivered under the appropriate clearance and NDA” |
| Custom study | **Commercial support and integration**. Embedding Kshana in the customer's toolchain, custom scenarios and priority fixes. | README.md:1524 “Commercial support & integration — embedding Kshana in your toolchain, custom scenarios, and priority fixes.” |
| Custom study | **Training and consulting**. Training and consulting on quantum and classical positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) performance analysis. | README.md:1542 “Training & consulting on quantum/classical PNT performance analysis.” |
| Free core | **Commercial licence of the open core (dual licence, not Pro)**. The same open-core code under a commercial licence for closed or proprietary integration without Affero General Public License (AGPL) obligations. Listed beside Pro because buyers ask for it there, but the public source ties it to the open core. | web/index.html:751 (branch HEAD 7f5e3e39) “free under the AGPL-3.0 (or a commercial licence for closed/proprietary use)” |
